# J121 five complete floating checkpoints

Each block contains the complete original binary64 input array serialized as decimal JSON with Python's round-trip float representation. It is a NEW compact input file, not the original full .last.json byte object: only the consumed n field is retained, with no coordinate omitted or changed. The source tools read only n. Statistics, timestamps and optimizer histories are not reconstruction dependencies. Numerical input identity does not assert a rational exact census.

Use the original run commands and source units in [internal-source-reference] and [internal-source-reference], replacing the corresponding original filename by the complete frozen filename below. The first array is the exact consumed paired_Q_qp endpoint before G8 rounding; it is the input to the relay scout and both nonlinear runs. The next two are the actual physical and polar relay inputs consumed by the two60-step continuations. The fourth preserves the20-accepted-step P checkpoint from the time-limited run, not a terminal80-step result. The fifth preserves the fragmented max-min negative control, not a target. Hashes refer to each JSON code block including its final newline.

The first/Qpair rounded G8 body and the two final relay G8 bodies are separately exact-recoverable from [internal-source-reference]. Numerical output files containing wall-clock times are not expected to replay byte-for-byte. Exact rational input/audit hashes are the separate certified output identities.
